requirements.R1: For each supported exact-input swap, collect floor(gross output / 100) units of the output ERC20 and credit floor(fee / 2) rebate units to the payer identified by the dedicated router.
requirements.R2: A user's cumulative claims for a pool and currency must not exceed their cumulative earned rebate for that pool and currency.
requirements.R3: Claims from a pool must not consume reserves owed to another pool. No pool's cumulative payments may exceed its collected fees.
requirements.R4: Only PoolManager can invoke the active hook callback, and only the dedicated router can identify a swap payer. A user can claim only their own credit.
requirements.R5: A rejected claim changes no balances or accounting. A failed token transfer atomically rolls back accounting.

environment_assumptions_pending_review: Two local initialized pools share the same two test ERC20 tokens and hook; no native currency or exact-output swaps.
Tokens are exact-transfer, non-rebasing and have no callbacks. The local router has no slippage protection and is not a production router.
The abstract Lean model covers one currency and one recipient per pool with nonnegative unbounded integers; AMM math, EVM arithmetic and token behavior are not modeled.
The PoolManager supplies actual output deltas. Fee collection in Lean is an input derived from Solidity replay, not a proof of swap math.
Remaining fees are retained by the hook. There is no admin withdrawal, upgrade mechanism, or live patch deployment.
open_questions: Creator approval of the 1% fee, 50% rebate, per-swap rounding, and retained-fee policy.
Whether a future challenge should support multiple modeled recipients, native currency, exact-output swaps, or adversarial tokens.
